title: All class 4 cellular automata are expected to be universal

fields.label: Label
fields.value: All class 4 cellular automata are expected to be universal

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Any cellular automaton showing class 4 behavior (localized structures moving and interacting in complicated ways) will, like rule 110, turn out to be universal, because such rules eventually yield localized structures rich enough to support universality.

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: I strongly suspect that it is true in general that any cellular automaton which shows overall class 4 behavior will turn out—like rule 110—to be universal.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci A New Kind of Science claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Stephen Wolfram, A New Kind of Science (Champaign, IL: Wolfram Media, 2002), Chapter 11, “The Notion of Computation”; section “Class 4 Behavior and Universality” (from p. 691), p. 691. Scope: class 4 cellular automata

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on wolfram2002-ch11-17: needs-new-data, resolvability 0.42

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing examples can support searches but do not settle the implication. Resolution requires a new general theorem or counterexample and a precise class-4 definition.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Formalize class 4 by asymptotic dynamical criteria and prove that every cellular automaton satisfying them can simulate a universal machine, or exhibit a rigorously class-4 nonuniversal counterexample.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Class 4 lacks a single rigorous definition.

No finite simulation can confirm the universal quantifier.

Universality is undecidable in broad cellular-automaton classes.

fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.2

data existence: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Universality is settled for rule 110 and for some two-dimensional class-4 rules such as the Game of Life, so particular cases are checkable. The claim is about every class-4 rule, and each new proof is a research project rather than a standard analysis. A single rigorously non-universal class-4 rule would refute it, but no such classification exists for the class as a whole.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Define class 4 by persistent, interacting, localized structures on a quiescent or periodic background. Confirm the claim only if every such rule has a universality proof, and refute it by one class-4 rule proved incapable of emulating a Turing machine.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Class 4 is diagnosed from pictures, so borderline rules can be labeled either way.

Not finding a glider computer does not prove that a class-4 rule is not universal.
